title: Voting Eligibility Checker
description: An election portal checks whether a person is eligible to vote. A person is eligible only if their age is 18 or above.
operation: Compare the age with the voting age limit: age >= 18

guide.input: Drag an Input node, open ⚙ and type 20 in Input Data (the person's age).
mapping: Input → Compare. Open Compare ⚙: set Operator = >= and Value = 18 (the voting age limit). Compare answers True when the age is 18 or more, otherwise False.
Compare → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show True (eligible to vote).

title: BMI Calculator
description: A fitness app calculates a person's Body Mass Index: BMI = Weight (kg) / Height² (m), rounded to 1 decimal place.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"weight": 70, "height": 1.75}.
mapping: Input → Get #1 (Key = weight is already filled in). This picks out the weight, 70.
Input → Get #2 (Key = height is already filled in) → Square. Square multiplies the height by itself: 1.75 × 1.75 = 3.0625.
Now build the division IN THIS ORDER: first connect Get #1 (weight) → Divide, then connect Square → Divide. Divide always does (first input) ÷ (second input) = 70 ÷ 3.0625.
Divide → Round (Decimals = 1 is already filled in) → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 22.9.

title: Palindrome String Checker
description: Given a word, check if it reads the same backward as forward (a palindrome).
operation: Check if the word is equal to its reverse

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to radar.
mapping: Input → Reverse. Reverse turns radar into radar backwards (here the same word).
Input → Compare (this carries the original word straight to Compare).
Reverse → Compare (this carries the reversed word). Open Compare ⚙ and set Operator = ==. Compare checks whether the two words are equal.
Compare → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show True (it is a palindrome).

title: Fahrenheit to Celsius Converter
description: A weather app converts a temperature reading from Fahrenheit to Celsius. Formula: C = (F - 32) × 5 / 9.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to 98.6 (the temperature in °F).
mapping: Input → Convert. The Convert block already contains the formula (F - 32) × 5 / 9, so there is nothing to set.
Convert → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 37.0 (the temperature in °C).

title: Average of Numbers
description: Given a list of numbers, calculate their average (mean) value: the sum of the numbers divided by how many numbers there are.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to [10, 20, 30, 40].
mapping: Input → Sum. Sum adds all the numbers: 10 + 20 + 30 + 40 = 100.
Input → Length. Length counts the numbers: 4.
Build the division IN THIS ORDER: first connect Sum → Divide, then connect Length → Divide. Divide does (first input) ÷ (second input) = 100 ÷ 4.
Divide → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 25.0.

title: Binary Search Locator
description: Given a sorted array and a target value, find the index of the target using Binary Search: look at the middle value and keep halving the search range.
operation: Binary search: Midpoint → Compare → Repeat on the half that can still contain the target

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"array": [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14], "target": 10}.
mapping: Input → Midpoint. Midpoint picks the middle index of the search range (here index 3, the value 8).

Midpoint → BinaryCompare. It compares the middle value with the target: equal = found; target smaller = search the left half; target larger = search the right half. (8 < 10, so the right half is next.)

BinaryCompare → RepeatSearch. It repeats Midpoint + Compare on the narrowed range until the target is found, and returns its index (10 is at index 4). It returns -1 when the target is not in the array.
RepeatSearch → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 4 (the index of the value 10).

title: Leap Year Checker
description: Given a year, decide whether it is a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except century years (divisible by 100), which must also be divisible by 400.
operation: Divisible by 4? Then, if it is a century year, divisible by 400?

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to 2000 (the year).
mapping: Input → Div4Check. It checks whether the year is divisible by 4 (2000 ÷ 4 → yes).
Div4Check → CenturyRule. If the year is a century year (divisible by 100) it must ALSO be divisible by 400 to stay a leap year (2000 ÷ 400 → yes). Years that are not centuries pass automatically.
CenturyRule → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show True (2000 is divisible by 4, by 100 and by 400).

title: Sorting a List of Numbers
description: Given an unsorted list of numbers, sort them in ascending order using Bubble Sort: repeatedly compare neighbouring numbers and swap them when the left one is greater than the right one.
operation: Bubble sort: compare & swap neighbours, repeat the pass until no swaps are left

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to [64, 25, 12, 22, 11].
mapping: Input → CompareSwap. It makes ONE pass over the list: each pair of neighbours is compared and swapped if the left number is greater (64 bubbles to the end: [25, 12, 22, 11, 64]).
CompareSwap → PassRepeat. It keeps repeating the pass until a full pass needs no swaps - then the list is sorted.
PassRepeat → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show [11, 12, 22, 25, 64].

title: Monthly Expense Pie Chart
description: A personal finance app records monthly expenses in 4 categories: Rent, Food, Transport and Entertainment. Calculate each category's percentage share of the total spending, then draw the result as a pie chart.
operation: Total = sum of all amounts; percentage = amount ÷ total × 100; draw a pie chart

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"Rent": 12000, "Food": 6000, "Transport": 3000, "Entertainment": 3000}.
mapping: Input → TotalSum. It adds up every category (total = 24000) and passes the amounts on.
TotalSum → Percentage. For every category it does amount ÷ total × 100 (Rent: 12000 ÷ 24000 × 100 = 50%).
Percentage → PieChart. It draws one slice per category (the chart title is already filled in).
PieChart → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must draw the pie chart and show Rent: 50% | Food: 25% | Transport: 12.5% | Entertainment: 12.5%. The reference picture shows how the chart should look.

title: Weekly Sales Bar Chart
description: A store tracks daily sales for 5 days against a fixed sales target of $200. Mark each day as "Above Target" (sales ≥ target) or "Below Target", then draw the results as a bar chart (green = Above, red = Below).
operation: For each day: sales ≥ target → Above Target, otherwise Below Target; draw a bar chart
expected_output: Mon: Below Target | Tue: Above Target | Wed: Above Target | Thu: Below Target | Fri: Above Target

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"sales": [180, 220, 250, 150, 300], "target": 200}. The days Mon-Fri are added automatically in order.
mapping: Input → TargetCompare. For each day it checks sales ≥ target (180 → Below, 220 → Above, 250 → Above, 150 → Below, 300 → Above).
TargetCompare → BarChart. It draws one bar per day: green for Above Target, red for Below Target (the chart title is already filled in).
BarChart → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must draw the bar chart and show Mon: Below Target | Tue: Above Target | Wed: Above Target | Thu: Below Target | Fri: Above Target.

title: Student Grade Distribution Pie Chart
description: Given a list of student scores, give each score a grade (A: 90 or more, B: 75-89, C: 50-74, F: below 50), count how many students got each grade, and draw the distribution as a pie chart.
operation: Score → grade; count the students per grade; draw a pie chart

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to [95, 82, 67, 45, 88, 91, 60].
mapping: Input → GradeClassifier. It turns every score into a grade (95 → A, 82 → B, 67 → C, 45 → F, 88 → B, 91 → A, 60 → C).
GradeClassifier → CountGrades. It counts the students in each grade: A 2, B 2, C 2, F 1.
CountGrades → PieChart. It draws one slice per grade (the chart title is already filled in).
PieChart → Output.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must draw the pie chart and show A: 2 | B: 2 | C: 2 | F: 1.
